title: ytdlp-web-player values
description: additionalProperties is false on every level this chart owns, so a key the chart does not read is rejected at render time instead of being silently ignored (#68). Two kinds of object stay open: the ones passed verbatim into the pod spec (probes, security contexts, ports, free-form annotations), because Kubernetes owns their schema - and the whole oauth2-proxy block, because that schema belongs to the subchart. Closing the latter would mean re-declaring somebody else's values and rejecting every key they add next release.

global.description: Helm's conventional cross-chart values. Unused by this chart, kept open so an umbrella install cannot break on it - and note that with a subchart present this is no longer hypothetical: whatever is set here reaches oauth2-proxy too.

oauth2ProxySecretRef.description: op:// item path for the proxy credentials; the item must carry the fields client-id, client-secret and cookie-secret. Read only while the proxy is enabled and still points at the Secret this chart renders.

ports.description: Rendered verbatim as the container's ports list; kept open because the chart does not interpret the entries. It does read one thing out of them: the entry named "http" carries the port that becomes PORT, the Service target and every probe target. A list without it fails the render with that message.

storage.description: The two emptyDirs. Deliberately not null-safe: an erased block means both size caps are unset, which is also the default, so nothing silent can happen here.

enabled.description: Gates this chart's whole Ingress template (#93). Here it frees BOTH domain and clusterIssuer: nothing outside the Ingress template reads either of them - the application needs no hostname of its own, so the searxng/matrix-synapse case of a domain read from an env block does not arise (guideline 1, checked in templates/ and in values.yaml).

annotations.description: Extra Ingress annotations, merged with the cert-manager annotation the chart always sets. Free-form keys by nature, so this object stays open.

oauth2-proxy.description: Values of the oauth2-proxy subchart, passed straight through. Open on purpose and at every level: this chart owns neither the keys nor their meaning, and a closed copy would reject whatever the subchart adds in its next release - the exact failure mode a schema is supposed to prevent, only pointed at the wrong chart. This chart reads exactly three of them: enabled (the dependency condition), ingress.enabled and ingress.hosts (the two-Ingress guard).

resources.description: May be null / empty: the chart then falls back to its default requests and computed limits (#99) instead of rendering a container without resource accounting.

resourceList.description: Both spellings of the ephemeral-storage key are accepted because the resources helper normalizes camelCase to the Kubernetes key.

securityContext.description: May be null / empty at any level: the chart then falls back to its hardening defaults (#99) instead of rendering an unhardened workload. The fallback reproduces THIS chart's defaults, including its pinned non-root uid for a root-by-default image (guideline 4).

pod.description: Merged onto the chart's pod hardening defaults and rendered as the pod's securityContext; kept open because the chart does not interpret the individual fields.

container.description: Merged onto the chart's container hardening defaults and rendered as the container's securityContext; kept open because the chart does not interpret the individual fields.

probe.description: Merged onto the chart's probe defaults and rendered as a container probe; kept open because the chart does not interpret the individual fields. May be null / empty, which means the defaults apply (#99) rather than the probe disappearing. The defaults carry the probe's context - the port NAME "http", so a changed container port moves the probes with it.
